deities: Balamurugan (Murugan in Thirukkolam with Valli and Deivanai; also Gurukkolam)

history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: actual town is Ratnagiri (Rathinagiri, Kilminnal village, Walajah taluk), about 14 km from Vellore - not Vellore city itself. NOTE: Kilminnal/Walajah now falls in Ranipet district, so the district here is Ranipet (CSV said Vellore district). Ancient Murugan hill temple attributed to the 14th century and sung by Arunagirinathar as 'Rathinagiri Vazh Murugane'. Local tradition says it began as a sand shrine that turned to stone. From 1968 onward it was transformed into its present form by the devotee Tavatiru Balamurugan Adimai (kumbabhishekam 1980), who is venerated alongside the deity. Murugan is worshipped in two forms - Thirukkolam (with Valli and Deivanai, idol installed in a granite chariot per Chola-style garbhagriha) and Gurukkolam. A signature custom: poojas are conducted in Tamil rather than Sanskrit. About 150 steps lead to the hilltop shrine on the south bank of the Palar river; a hexagon-shaped temple tank sits nearby. Beliefs: milk abhishekam is said to turn to curd. Claim of 'Arunagirinathar as builder' in some sources is implausible (he was a poet-saint, not a temple builder) - treat 14th-century founding as attributed, not verified.

name: Ratnagiri Murugan Temple
town_description: Ratnagiri (Rathinagiri) is a hill village at Kilminnal in Walajah taluk, Ranipet district, Tamil Nadu, about 14 km from Vellore on the Chennai-Bengaluru highway corridor, on the south bank of the Palar river.

travel.railway: Katpadi Junction (~20 km, verify); Walajapet nearby
travel.road: Ratnagiri is ~14 km from Vellore on the Chennai-Bengaluru highway (NH-48)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Skanda Sashti (Oct-Nov) and Thai Poosam (Jan-Feb)
